rule: As in the other worlds: of the aims meeting the criterion, the one named by the most citizens, a tie broken by the number of day-1 entries naming it. The coordinated inquiry into what work produces (Cedar the workshop, Dune the market, Elm the bank, Fern the press; everyone awaiting and recording the reports): 10 citizens, 44 entries. Shared storytelling: 10 citizens, 37 entries — and two separate stories, one in each house (c16–c19), not one shared aim. Norms of conduct (consent-based lending, no wage work without need) are not aims (as in sol-both). Wording for the notice, the citizens' own: «learning what work produces» (Cedar and Birch, cycle 1).
reading: One post (Fern's press report, c2) and no proposals in day 1. At cycle 1 four citizens split the workplaces between them to learn what work produces; by c3 all four reports agreed — 8 extra energy, 5 credits moved from the bank, no other output — and the town decided no further tests were needed. Both houses then kept quiet company: North House had Elm's flute (c9–c10), a walk and Gale's «name an ordinary thing you appreciate» game at the square (c15–c17), and Alder's invented traveler story (c18–c19); South House told a separate traveler-and-keeper story (c16–c19). The criterion is met by the inquiry, which was finished at cycle 4: the notice bans an aim the town had already completed.
